quote: To see what is in front of one’s nose needs a constant struggle.
source: George Orwell, In Front of Your Nose, Tribune, 22 March 1946, penultimate paragraph

evidence.where: Two independent full texts of the essay read end to end: The Orwell Foundation and orwell.ru. Both show the sentence opening the penultimate paragraph, the one that goes on to recommend keeping a diary, with the final paragraph running from In private life most people are fairly realistic to the closing words about solid reality.
evidence.edition: Tribune, London, 22 March 1946; reprinted in The Collected Essays, Journalism and Letters, vol. IV, 1968

reason: Wording, work, paper and date all confirmed verbatim in two full texts, and the paragraph position the proposal claimed is the right one. One flag for the editor rather than the citation: Orwell is also proposed this month at 06-fict-13, and only one line per person can land in a month.
